note: Choose a path before anything changes. Each decision lists what it costs, what it buys and what it needs from you. Status values: implemented = done in this pass and reversible; needs decision = waiting on you; blocked = waiting on an account, a person or a provider. Reply with a suggestion ID and an option letter, for example 'S-01 B'.

options.label: Keep tagged /dp/ links on the observed products, marked as pending validation (current).
options.tradeoff: Readers can click now; the links are not yet validated in Associates Central.

options.label: Hide all buy buttons until gate G-02 passes.
options.tradeoff: Safer for compliance; the site has no paths to purchase until the owner tests.

suggestions.why: The single biggest compliance risk on the site.
suggestions.note: Option B until gate G-02 passes.

options.label: One new guide every two weeks (proposed default).
options.tradeoff: Steady growth; needs a writing slot every two weeks.

options.label: One new guide per week.
options.tradeoff: Faster growth; higher manual load.

options.label: A batch of 10 guides before launch, then monthly.
options.tradeoff: Meets the 'at least 10 posts' rule of thumb (S11) sooner.

suggestions.recommendation: C, to reach the 10-post rule of thumb before the Associates review.
suggestions.why: Cadence decides how fast the site looks alive to a reviewer.
suggestions.note: Pick a cadence you can keep for a month.

options.label: Self-host tools/collector.mjs on a small VPS you control, behind HTTPS.
options.tradeoff: Full control of raw data; you run the server.

options.label: Run the collector on a platform that supports Node.js with persistent storage.
options.tradeoff: Less server work; check the platform's data terms.

options.label: Use a third-party privacy-focused analytics product.
options.tradeoff: Quickest setup; a separate processor, so it needs its own disclosure.

options.label: No analytics for now (current).
options.tradeoff: Nothing to maintain; no click or conversion data.

suggestions.recommendation: A or B if you want measured queries before choosing the next topic.
suggestions.why: No click data until a receiver exists.
suggestions.note: The receiver must be HTTPS and outside this repository.

options.label: Keep the working name 'Affil3' (current).
options.tradeoff: Matches the repository.

options.label: Choose a consumer-facing name and domain.
options.tradeoff: Better recall; needs a domain and a naming check.

suggestions.why: Brand name is already in use across titles, feed and sitemap.
suggestions.note: Changing it later means a redirect plan.

options.label: Typography and layout only, no product photos (current).
options.tradeoff: Avoids use of Program Content outside the Associates purpose (S02).

options.label: Original photography of products you own.
options.tradeoff: Strong for reader trust; needs equipment and time.

options.label: Amazon-supplied images through the Associates tools.
options.tradeoff: Allowed only as Program Content on your site; needs review against the IP License.

suggestions.recommendation: B for guides; A for the front page.
suggestions.why: Illustrations are decorative and cannot be mistaken for the product being sold.
suggestions.note: Product photography needs the Creators/PA API.

options.label: Team byline 'Affil3 editorial team' (current).
options.tradeoff: No invented person.

options.label: Named author with a real bio and a review date.
options.tradeoff: Stronger signal of accountability; needs a real person.

suggestions.recommendation: B once a real reviewer is named.
suggestions.why: A named author is a trust signal and a policy answer.
suggestions.note: Requires a real person and their consent.

options.label: Publish the 5 existing guides, then add more on the cadence chosen in S-02 (current).
options.tradeoff: Fewer than the 10-post rule of thumb at launch (FLG-007).

options.label: Hold the site from review until 10 original posts exist.
options.tradeoff: Aligns with S11; delays the tag-based program.

suggestions.why: Content depth is what an Associates reviewer looks at.
suggestions.note: Ten guides is a rule of thumb, not a guarantee.

options.label: A gift and holiday-cooking guide hub for November and December 2026.
options.tradeoff: Seasonal relevance; needs a first-party reason to rank it, and no trend data is in hand.

options.label: Evergreen guides only (current).
options.tradeoff: Simpler; no seasonal claims.

suggestions.recommendation: B until measured queries (from S-03) show interest.
suggestions.note: Every dated claim must be re-checked or removed.

options.label: Keep four clusters: air fryers, air fryer ovens, thermometers, unresolved (current).
options.tradeoff: Reflects the five links; the 'unresolved' cluster is a holding area.

options.label: Focus on air fryers and move the thermometer to a supporting note.
options.tradeoff: Tighter topic; drops the thermometer cluster.

suggestions.recommendation: A until the unresolved link is decided.
suggestions.why: Three clusters match the five submitted products.
suggestions.note: A fourth cluster has no products to support it.

options.label: Show no prices or ratings (current).
options.tradeoff: No stale or unverified numbers.

options.label: Show dated prices from an authorized source, refreshed on a schedule.
options.tradeoff: Useful to buyers; needs an authorized data source and a refresh process (the Associates tools or PA-API access). Not set up here.

suggestions.recommendation: A now; B only after an authorized source is confirmed.
suggestions.why: Prices and ratings are the fastest way to break the rules if done by hand.
suggestions.note: Only via Creators/PA API, and only if you accept the maintenance.

options.label: No email capture (current).
options.tradeoff: No email data to store.

options.label: Opt-in email list.
options.tradeoff: Direct reach; check the Trademark Guidelines (no Amazon Marks in email, S02) and the Program Policies for email before any Amazon link is sent.

suggestions.recommendation: A until the email rules are reviewed.
suggestions.why: Reader capture needs a provider, consent language and a privacy notice.
suggestions.note: No email form is published until that exists.

options.label: Do not connect Search Console.
options.tradeoff: No search data.

options.label: Verify the site in Search Console and submit the sitemap after deploy (recommended).
options.tradeoff: Needs a Google account owner (Q-12).

suggestions.why: Search Console is how the next topic stops being a guess.
suggestions.note: Requires account access for the verified property.

suggestions.why: The earlier front page opened with method language. A reader decides in seconds whether this looks like a shop.
suggestions.note: Reversible: the previous layout is in git history.

options.label: Keep the earlier, audit-style front page.
options.tradeoff: Nothing to review; it reads like a report, not a publication.

options.label: Publication front page: illustrated hero, five product cards, guides, categories, then the records in the footer.
options.tradeoff: Warmer and easier to act on; the verification detail moves one click deeper.

options.label: Hire a designer and rebuild from a Figma file.
options.tradeoff: Best possible finish; slower, and needs a budget and a brief.

suggestions.recommendation: B, with A kept in git history so it can be restored.

suggestions.why: Buyers compare before they click. A comparison table is the cheapest page that answers 'which one'.
suggestions.note: Every cell is the listing title wording; nothing is inferred.

options.label: Add a side-by-side comparison of the tracked products, quoting the listing titles.
options.tradeoff: Useful and honest, but it shows how thin unverified data is.

options.label: Wait for API data before publishing any comparison.
options.tradeoff: No comparison page for now; nothing to maintain.

suggestions.recommendation: A. A comparison of what the listing states is still useful, as long as it is labelled that way.

suggestions.why: Search engines index pages, not table rows. Each product needs its own URL to rank for its own name.
suggestions.note: Five pages, generated from the same register as the shop table.

options.label: One page per tracked product: observed listing, sources, what is unverified, related guides.
options.tradeoff: Five more pages to keep current when a listing changes.

options.label: Keep products inside the shop table only.
options.tradeoff: Nothing to maintain; almost nothing for a search engine to rank.

suggestions.recommendation: A, with the observation date printed on every page.

suggestions.why: The repository publishes three parallel publications on the same topics. That splits whatever search signal exists and can look like duplicate content.
suggestions.note: Robots.txt disallows /editorial/ and /legacy/, and every /editorial/ page now carries a noindex meta tag. Nothing was deleted.

options.label: One indexable site at the root; the other two publications stay online but out of the index.
options.tradeoff: The archive is still readable by anyone with the link, but not searchable.

options.label: Publish all three and let search engines choose.
options.tradeoff: Faster to do nothing; weaker and harder to explain.

options.label: Delete the extra publications.
options.tradeoff: Cleanest for search; destroys the other sessions' verification passes and their provenance.

suggestions.recommendation: A. It keeps every verification pass readable while giving search engines a single site.

suggestions.why: Three new guides close the thermometer and oven clusters, and each one links to the product pages it can help with.
suggestions.note: Eight guides now. Cadence is still S-02.

options.label: Add three cluster-closing guides and link the clusters both ways.
options.tradeoff: More pages to keep dated and corrected.

options.label: Publish nothing new until the policy questions close.
options.tradeoff: Safest; the site stays at five guides.

suggestions.recommendation: A. Guides are the lowest-risk asset here: they carry no product claims.

suggestions.topic: Product data through an Amazon API
suggestions.why: Prices, ratings, availability and images can only be shown lawfully through Amazon-served content or the Creators/PA API.
suggestions.note: Requires an active account with qualifying sales. Not available to this build.

options.label: Keep the site API-free: no prices, ratings, availability or product photography.
options.tradeoff: Thinner pages, but nothing to break and nothing to misstate.

options.label: Apply for Creators/PA API access and render only API-served data.
options.tradeoff: Richer pages; a new failure mode and an eligibility bar you have not met yet.

suggestions.recommendation: A now, B once the account has qualifying sales.

suggestions.why: A dated seasonal page can earn links, but every dated claim has to be re-checked or removed.
suggestions.note: No seasonal page is published yet; nothing claims a current promotion.

options.label: Publish a seasonal hub with dates and a re-check owner.
options.tradeoff: Needs a calendar and a person to keep it true.

options.label: Skip seasonal pages until a cadence exists (current).
options.tradeoff: No seasonal traffic; no stale claims.

suggestions.recommendation: B until S-02 is settled, then A with a named re-check owner.

paths.name: Ship and measure
paths.summary: Keep the current tagged links live, close gate G-02 in Associates Central this week, and add only Search Console.
needs: Owner runs one Special Link per product in Associates Central (Q-04)
Owner confirms the tracking ID belongs to the account (Q-03)
buys: A live site readers can act on today
First real search data in about two weeks
risks: Untested Special Links stay live until G-02 closes
No click counts until an analytics receiver exists

paths.name: Measure first
paths.summary: Deploy the collector, record the five events for two weeks, then choose the next topic from data instead of instinct.
needs: An HTTPS receiver for tools/collector.mjs (S-03 A/B)
A privacy notice covering the click counter (Q-13)
A fixed test window and a known set of test clicks (D-06)
buys: Click and outbound data before more writing
A defensible answer to 'what should we publish next'
risks: More setup before any content ships
Raw analytics becomes personal data if the receiver is misconfigured

paths.name: Associates-ready
paths.summary: Hide buy buttons until G-02 passes, reach ten guides, then submit the site for review with a clean disclosure trail.
needs: Option B on S-01 (hide buy buttons)
Option C or B on S-02 (batch to ten guides)
Owner confirmation that the account declares this site (Q-03)
buys: A content base that meets the 'robust content' rule of thumb
risks: No purchase path while buttons are hidden
